title: Finals Exam Reviewer
description: Modules 10–14: Code Reuse and Class Hierarchy, Interfaces, Abstract Class and Interface, Polymorphism, and Modularity. Multiple choice + output tracing.

questions.question: By allowing information of a superclass to be taken on by subclasses, the information is said to be:
options: Duplicated in every object
Hidden from the subclass
Deleted from the superclass
Reused at the subclass level
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Which statement describes changes to software specification?
options: Changes affect only the user interface
Changes are only allowed before coding
Changes to software specification are inevitable
Changes to software specification never happen
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the situations discussed for changes in a class hierarchy?
options: Change in the operating system for some subclasses
Change in property definition for some subclasses
Change in the programming language for all subclasses
Change in the compiler used by the superclass
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. The three situations: change for all subclasses, change for some subclasses, and adding/deleting a class.

questions.question: If inheritance is NOT available, a change in the representation of employee number must be made:
options: Individually in every relevant class, which may lead to inconsistency
Automatically by the compiler for every class that uses it
Only in main(), since attributes are defined there for all classes
Only once, in the Employee class, and it propagates to every subclass
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: If inheritance IS available, a change in the representation of employee number is limited to the:
options: Last subclass created, and it propagates to the superclass
Manager class, and it is copied to the other subclasses
Employee (super)class, and it propagates to the subclasses
main() method, and it is passed to every class
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Defining a property once in the superclass and letting subclasses inherit it results in:
options: Uniform and consistent property definitions and minimal redundancy
Different property definitions and more redundancy in each subclass
Inconsistent definitions that must be repeated at the subclass level
Harder maintenance, since every subclass must be changed separately
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: In the HomeCare example, the manager's pay was wrong because:
options: The Manager class had no constructor, so the basic salary was never set at all
The secretary's salary was added to it, since both classes share getPay() in Employee
The commission was counted twice, since Manager also extends SalesPerson in the hierarchy
The allowance was omitted, since getPay() in Employee returns only the basic salary
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: What is the disadvantage of removing getPay() from Employee and defining it individually in every subclass?
options: The program cannot compile, because getPay() must exist in the Employee superclass
The definition is repeated in all subclasses, which is inefficient and hard to maintain
Subclasses can no longer have constructors, so the objects cannot be created at all
Each subclass inherits two getPay() methods, which causes conflicts at run time
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Which approach to fixing the manager's pay is better?
options: Keep getPay() in Employee and redefine it in the Manager class
Remove the Manager class from the hierarchy
Compute the pay inside main() for every employee
Remove getPay() from Employee and define it in every subclass
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. It enhances software reuse and minimizes the effect of change on other classes.

questions.question: A redefining method has the same method name and parameter definition as the redefined method, but:
options: It must have more parameters
It must have a different name
It cannot return a value
Its implementation may differ
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: When adding a new class into an existing class hierarchy, it is always recommended that the new class be created as a:
options: Superclass of all existing classes
Separate program
Subclass in the class hierarchy
Copy of an existing class
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: To add the new Triangle class to the Shape program, which of the following is involved?
options: Change the getName() method of every existing class
Create a new Triangle class as a subclass of Shape
Rewrite the Circle and Square classes
Delete the Shape class
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Subclassing is a desired design practice in object-oriented software engineering because:
options: It prevents code reuse
It has minimal impact on software maintenance
It removes the need for constructors in subclasses
It makes every attribute public
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Subclassing is specialization.

questions.question: Deleting subclasses that are NOT superclasses to other classes:
options: Requires rewriting the superclass
Breaks every other class in the class hierarchy
Has a minimal impact on software maintenance
Is not allowed in Java
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: In the Shape example, the name attribute is declared private, so other objects get its value through:
options: Direct access to the name variable from any class
The main() method, which stores the name for others
The calculateArea() method defined in each subclass
The getName() method defined in the Shape class
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Trace the output (Redefining getPay()): what does this program print?
questions.answer:
Simon has a pay of 11000
Selene has a pay of 2500
Charmaine has a pay of 1200
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Manager redefines getPay() (same name and parameters), so its version adds the allowance; Secretary and Clerk inherit Employee's getPay().

questions.question: Trace the output (Constructor chain with super()): what does this program print?
questions.answer:
Person created
Employee created
Technician created
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. super() runs the parent constructor first, so the messages print from the top of the hierarchy down.

questions.question: Trace the output (Adding Triangle to the hierarchy): what does this program print?
questions.answer:
Square S: 9.0
Triangle T: 10.0
Shape X: 0.0
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. calculateArea() returns a float, so the int area 9 prints as 9.0. Triangle was added as a subclass, so Shape and Square did not change.

questions.question: The capability to inherit from more than one class is called:
options: Multiple inheritance
Encapsulation
Single inheritance
Polymorphism
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Which of the following languages allows a subclass to inherit from more than one parent class?
options: Java
Both C++ and Java
Neither C++ nor Java
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Why is multiple inheritance prohibited in Java?
options: Interfaces are slower than classes, so Java limits each class to one parent
Parent classes may have identical names, and super() would be unclear with multiple parents
Constructors are not allowed in Java subclasses, so super() cannot be called
Java does not support classes with parents, so only interfaces can be inherited by a subclass
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: A class inheriting from a superclass that has inherited from another superclass represents:
options: Single inheritance with multiple generations
Multiple inheritance through an interface
Multiple inheritance with a single generation
An anonymous inner class with two parents
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Java's alternative to multiple inheritance is the:
options: Static variable
Abstract method
Package
Interface
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: In an interface, all methods (if any) are implicitly:
options: protected and final
public and static
public and abstract
private and static
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: In an interface, all data items (if any) are implicitly:
options: protected and static
public, static, and final
public and abstract
private and abstract
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: An interface is a description of:
options: What a class does, but not how it is done
The constructor of a class
The private data of a class
How a class does something, but not what it does
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Which keyword is placed in a class header to use an interface?
options: extends
super
interface
implements
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Whereas extends lets a subclass use nonprivate, nonoverridden members of its parent, implements requires the class to:
options: Inherit the parent's private data and methods
Call super() twice
Become an interface
Implement its own version of each method
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: The interface construct in Java is used with single inheritance to provide:
options: Some form of multiple inheritance
Some form of information hiding
Some form of static binding
Some form of operation overloading
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: class SalesManager extends SalesPerson implements Manage { ... } means that SalesManager:
options: Is derived from Manage and implements the SalesPerson interface
Cannot have a constructor
Is derived from SalesPerson and implements the Manage interface
Is an interface
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: In the Manage interface, authorize() is declared without a body. The SalesManager class must:
options: Call authorize() from the main() method only
Implement the abstract method authorize()
Declare authorize() as private
Remove authorize() from Manage
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Choosing between SalesManager as a subclass of SalesPerson or of Manager (with a CanTakeOrder interface) is:
options: A modeling problem resolved with more information on the problem domain and requirements
Not allowed in Java, because a class cannot implement an interface and extend a class
Always solved by using SalesPerson, because collectPayment() is already defined there
Decided automatically by the compiler based on which superclass has more methods
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: When a class implements Worker, it must include a work() method or else:
options: The class becomes an interface, and its descendants inherit work() from it
The Worker interface must be changed so that work() is no longer abstract
The program still runs, and Java creates an empty work() method automatically for the class
The class must be declared abstract, and its descendants must implement the method
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: A WorkingDog extends Dog and implements Worker. Which method is it required to contain because of implements Worker?
options: speak()
getHoursOfTraining()
work()
setName()
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Why make many classes implement the Worker interface instead of each just having a work() method?
options: The classes can share private data, because interfaces store each object's fields
You do not have to guess the name of the method that shows the work the objects perform
The classes no longer need constructors, because the interface creates their objects
The classes run faster, because interface methods are bound at compile time only
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: A class that implements an interface represents a situation similar to inheritance. A WorkingDog therefore:
options: "Is a" Dog and "is a" Worker, but it is not an Animal
"Is a" Worker, but it is no longer a Dog or an Animal
"Is an" Animal only, since interfaces do not count as types
"Is a" Dog, "is an" Animal, and "is a" Worker
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: What is the output of this program?
options: Woof! / I am a dog who works
The program does not compile, because Dog does not implement Worker
Woof! / Woof! / I am a dog who works
I am a dog who works / Woof!
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. Output: Woof! / Woof! / I am a dog who works. work() calls the inherited speak() first, so Woof! appears twice.

questions.question: Trace the output (One interface, many classes): what does this program print?
questions.answer:
Changing colors
Going to the next page
Flipping
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. The loop starts at index 1, so the first Pancake is skipped. Each class writes its own turn().

questions.question: Trace the output (extends and implements): what does this program print?
questions.answer:
Selling products
Authorizing discount
Selling products
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. sell() is inherited through extends; authorize() had to be written because of implements Manage.

questions.question: What happens with the statement Animal myPet = new Animal("Murphy"); if Animal is an abstract class?
options: The program does not compile, because no Animal objects can exist
It compiles, but speak() prints nothing because it has no method body
It creates a Dog object instead, because Dog extends the Animal class
It creates an Animal object normally, because the constructor exists
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: You create an abstract class such as Animal only so that you can:
options: Use it as a package
Extend it
Instantiate it
Hide it from subclasses
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: If you do not want to create Dog objects but want Dog to be a parent to further subclasses, then the Dog class:
options: Also must be abstract
Must be an interface
Must be private
Must be final
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: The @Override annotation for a method such as speak() is:
options: Used only in interfaces, never in subclasses
Not necessary, but it provides error checking and documentation
Used to create a new object of the parent class
Required, or the program will not compile at all without it
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Using the same method name to indicate different implementations is called:
options: Bundling
Encapsulation
Polymorphism
Static binding
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Data attributes declared in an interface construct are always:
options: protected and static
public and non-final
private and abstract
static and final
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Static because there is only one copy; final because they are not modifiable.

questions.question: Names for values with a specific meaning, such as RED = 1 in the Colourable interface, are called:
options: Packages
Constants
References
Parameters
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: All methods in an interface are:
options: Static methods that the implementing class may not override
Constructors that run when a class implements the interface
Private methods hidden from every class that uses the interface
Abstract methods that any class using the interface must implement
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Methods in an interface may NOT be static because:
options: Interfaces cannot contain methods, only constant data attributes
Static methods must have constructors, which interfaces do not have
Static methods, being class specific, are never abstract
Static methods are always private, so no class could call them
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: ColourTest implements Colourable but does not implement getColour(). How must ColourTest be declared?
options: abstract class ColourTest implements Colourable
interface ColourTest implements Colourable
static class ColourTest implements Colourable
final class ColourTest implements Colourable
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Why must setColour() in ColourTest be declared public?
options: Because ColourTest is declared abstract, all of its methods must be public
It is a method of the Colourable interface, and interface methods are public
Because main() is static, every method it can call must also be public
Because setColour() has a parameter, and methods with parameters must be public
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Abstract classes and interfaces are similar in that:
options: You cannot instantiate concrete objects from either one
A class can extend any number of either of them
Both must have constructors that create objects
Both can contain only private methods and private data fields
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Abstract classes differ from interfaces because:
options: Abstract classes cannot have variables, but interfaces can have any kind of variable
Interfaces can contain constructors and nonabstract methods, but abstract classes cannot
Interfaces can be instantiated with new, but abstract classes can never be instantiated
Abstract classes can contain nonabstract methods, but all interface methods must be abstract
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: A class can inherit from how many abstract superclasses, and implement how many interfaces?
options: None of either
Any number of abstract superclasses, but only one interface
Only one abstract superclass, but any number of interfaces
Only one of each
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: According to the comparison table, which is true about constructors?
options: Neither can ever have a constructor, because neither one can be instantiated with new
An interface has no constructor; an abstract class's constructor is invoked when a child object is instantiated
Both have constructors, and each constructor creates an object of its own type whenever it is called
An interface's constructor is called each time a class implements the interface
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: According to the comparison table, which is true about variables?
options: Interfaces cannot have any variables at all, while abstract classes must declare only private ones
Abstract class variables must be public, static, and final; interfaces have no restrictions
Both must declare all of their variables private, so that subclasses cannot change them
Interface variables must be public, static, and final; abstract classes have no restrictions on variables
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: An interface is generally used for achieving:
options: Multiple inheritance in Java
Faster compilation
Information hiding in packages
Static binding
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Given public abstract class LandVehicle { ... }, which statement is invalid?
options: LandVehicle l;
class Car extends LandVehicle { }
LandVehicle l = new LandVehicle();
LandVehicle[] list = new LandVehicle[3];
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Interface data fields must not be private because:
options: Private data cannot be static, and every field of an interface must be a static field
Private data uses too much memory, since every object would store its own copy of it
Interfaces are always final, so private fields would be hidden from the interface itself
Interface methods cannot contain method bodies, so there is no way to retrieve private data
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: The purpose of creating an interface containing constants is to:
options: Create objects of the interface so that each object holds its own separate copy of the values
Replace all the classes in a program with one interface that contains every method
Provide a set of data that a number of classes can use without having to redeclare the values
Hide the data from every class so that the values can never be read by any program
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: A class that has no name and is defined inside another class is a(n):
options: Anonymous inner class
Package
Interface
Abstract class
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: When defining an anonymous inner class, you:
options: Use the keyword implements, and declare the class outside the main class
Use the new operator and do not use the keywords extends or implements
Must give the class a name and save it in its own separate .java file
Must use the keyword extends, and give the class a name before using it
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: An anonymous inner class must either implement an interface or extend another class, and it must:
options: Be declared in a separate package from the class in which it is defined
Have at least two constructors that call the superclass default constructor
Override all the abstract methods in the interface or superclass
Be declared static so that it can be instantiated more than once in the program
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: A variable whose value is assigned only once, which an anonymous inner class may access, is called:
options: Abstract
Effectively final
Static
Protected and static
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: What is the output of this program?
options: GREENBLUE
The program does not compile, because RED, GREEN, and BLUE are not declared static
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Output: 5. Interface data attributes are implicitly public, static, and final.

questions.question: Trace the output (Constants in an interface): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Interface data are public, static and final constants. * runs before +, and once a String comes first, + joins text ("Colour " + 1 + 2 = Colour 12).

questions.question: Trace the output (Subclass of a class that implements an interface): what does this program print?
questions.answer:
in A.x
in B.z
in A.x
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. B inherits x() from A, which implements I, so a B object can also be used as an I.

questions.question: Trace the output (Abstract class with a concrete method): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. An abstract class cannot be instantiated, but it can have constructors and concrete methods; each concrete subclass must implement speak().

questions.question: The binding of variables to operations at compile time is known as:
options: Static binding
Run-time binding
Dynamic binding
Late binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: The binding of variables to operations at run time is known as:
options: Compile-time binding
Static binding
Dynamic binding
Early binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Which statement about static and dynamic binding is correct?
options: Static binding is limited and may lead to maintenance difficulty; dynamic binding provides design flexibility
Only procedural languages use dynamic binding
Both are identical
Static binding provides design flexibility; dynamic binding is limited and causes maintenance difficulty
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: In the procedural Shape example, why were calculateCircleArea() and calculateSquareArea() needed?
options: Java requires separate routine names for every shape, even in object-oriented code
The switch statement cannot call any routine that has the word Area in its name
Circles and squares use the same formula, so the names only make the code readable
Most procedural languages do not allow two routines to have the same name
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: With static binding, adding a new shape such as Triangle requires changes in:
options: No part of the program, since the switch statement detects new shapes on its own at run time
Multiple places (data section, switch statement, and routine section), which is error prone
Only the println statement, since the routine section does not need to change
Only one place: a new Triangle class, without touching the rest of the program
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: With dynamic binding, the appropriate calculateArea() method is selected based on:
options: The class of the shape referenced at run time
The name of the array
A switch statement written by the programmer
The order the methods were written
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Every SalariedEmployee "is an" Employee. Which statement is also true?
options: Superclass objects are members of all subclasses
An Employee is always an HourlyEmployee
Every Employee is a SalariedEmployee
An Employee is not necessarily a SalariedEmployee
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: A reference is not an object, but it:
options: Is always abstract
Points to a memory address
Is created with the keyword new
Contains all the object's methods
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Assigning a variable or constant of one type to a variable of another type is called:
options: Static binding, early binding, or fixed binding
Overloading, overriding, or redefining
Promotion, implicit conversion, or upcasting
Encapsulation, bundling, or information hiding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Using a reference polymorphically allows you to:
options: Extend a base class and use extended objects when a base class type is expected
Create objects of an abstract class directly by using the keyword new
Make all methods static so that they are bound when the program is compiled
Avoid writing subclasses, since one reference can hold every method
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: In Java, all instance method calls are virtual method calls by default. This means:
options: Methods cannot be overridden
Methods must be static
The method is chosen by the compiler before the program runs
The method used is determined when the program runs
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: An application's ability to select the correct subclass method depending on the argument type is known as:
options: Information hiding
Dynamic method binding
Static method binding
Operation overloading
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism. It is also called late method binding.

questions.question: In Java, which methods use dynamic binding and which use static binding?
options: All methods use dynamic binding
Class methods use dynamic binding; instance methods use static binding
Instance methods use dynamic binding; class methods use static binding
All methods use static binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Comparing the two kinds of binding:
options: Both are equally fast and flexible
Dynamic binding is not supported in Java
Dynamic binding makes programs flexible; static binding operates more quickly
Static binding makes programs flexible; dynamic binding operates more quickly
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Dynamic method binding is most useful when you want a method whose parameters:
options: Are always primitive types, such as int or double values
Might be one of several types, such as any Animal descendant
Cannot be objects, because objects are bound at compile time
Are always strings, so that the method can print their names
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: When you create an array of objects in Java, you are actually creating:
options: Space for references to objects
A new class
The objects themselves, already constructed
A package of objects
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Animal[] animalRef = new Animal[3]; Given that Animal is abstract, this statement:
options: Does not compile, because an array cannot be declared using an abstract type
Creates three Animal objects, one for each element of the animalRef array
Creates one Dog, one Cow, and one Snake object to fill the three array elements
Reserves memory for three Animal references without instantiating any Animal
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: An array of superclass references can hold subclass references:
options: Only if the superclass is concrete, never abstract
Only if the superclass is abstract, never concrete
Whether the superclass is abstract or concrete
Never, since every array element must be one type
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: The ability to use the same name for two or more methods in a class is known as:
options: Encapsulation
Operation overloading
Static binding
Polymorphism
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Two methods have the same method signature if:
options: Their names are the same and the number and type of formal parameters are the same
They have the same access specifier and are both declared static in their classes
They are declared in the same package and have the same number of statements inside
Their return types are the same, even if their names and parameters are different
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Given constructors A(), A(int x), A(int x, int y), and A(String x), which is called by new A("hello")?
options: A(int x)
A(int x, int y)
A(String x)
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Declaring two public void a1() {} methods in the same class is:
options: Valid overriding, because the second replaces the first
Valid overloading, because the two methods are separate
Valid only if one of the two methods is declared static
Invalid, reported as a duplicate method declaration
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Can the return type alone distinguish overloaded methods from one another?
options: Only for static methods declared in the same class
No, the return type does not distinguish overloaded methods
Only for methods that are declared in an interface
Yes, the return type alone always distinguishes them from each other
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Declaring methods of the same signature in different, unrelated classes is:
options: Valid in object-oriented programming
Allowed only for constructors
Invalid
Allowed only if the classes are abstract
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: For a subclass method to redefine (override) a superclass method:
options: The subclass method must have more parameters than the other
The superclass method must be private
The method signatures of the two methods must be the same
The methods must have different names
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: The ability of different objects to perform the appropriate method in response to the same message is known as:
options: Operation overloading
Modularity
Polymorphism
